claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game is locked to 60 frames per second by default.

citations.review_text:
I've put well over 500 hours into the PS5 version of Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain, and after recently deciding to give the PC version a try, I can honestly say it feels even better to play.

The gameplay is still some of the smoothest and most satisfying I've ever experienced. Whether you're sneaking through enemy outposts, calling in supply drops, or approaching missions however you want, everything feels incredibly responsive. The freedom the game gives you is something very few stealth games have managed to match.

On PC, the game feels fantastic, especially with the added precision of mouse and keyboard or the flexibility to use a controller. One thing I highly recommend is uncapping the frame rate. By default, the game is locked to 60 FPS, but removing that cap makes the experience feel even smoother if your hardware can handle it.

What impresses me the most is just how well this game has aged. Even though it's been out for a bit over 11 years, it still looks, plays, and feels like something that could have released around 2020. The visuals hold up incredibly well, the controls are still top-tier, and the gameplay loop remains as addictive as ever.

If you've never played Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain, you're missing one of the greatest stealth-action games ever made. And if you're returning to it on PC like I did, you're in for an even smoother experience.

Rating: 10/10

Really good game. Too bad it's locked to 60 FPS, but it's less annoying under Linux / SteamOS than it was under Windows in the past with a 4090 RTX. What I think is pretty interesting. Despite all this, I definitly can recommend it.

citations.review_text:
MGS 5 brings a great stealth experience. 
All though in my opinion it doesn't compare to Metal Gear Solid 1 the original, it still holds its own for the style. 
This game is more for the NEW AGE mgs fans with smoother controls & gameplay with also the Open world aspect. 
There's ALOT you can do for side missions as well to keep your mind fresh & add more to your personal base. 
KEEP IN MIND.. for those who played the O.G... its NOTHING LIKE THAT as that came out for PS1. 

The only downside is MOST if not all voice coms from enemies are in "RUSSIAN" dialogue. BUT it gives the player English subtitles. 

This game will bring your stealthing gameplay to life in ways that will test you no matter how good you are at COD.  

If you are looking for awesome graphics, great gameplay, replay value & stealth testing .. THIS IS THE GAME FOR YOU!!! Though IF you get the chance,.. you may want to play "GROUND ZERO" first.

citations.review_text:
gameplay was enjoyable until they started forcing you to repeat missions on hard mode just to progress the story. online mode forces you to gimp your base or pay konami to skip the grind. the open world is lifeless and has nothing fun to do outside of main missions.
I was ok with that. I was willing to tolerate that.
suddenly updating your game YEARS later after complete radio silence just to make it run worse and break mods? yeah no it's not worth it anymore.
just watch the cutscene compilation on youtube and maybe some 'funny moments' videos from 7-8 years ago, you'll get more enjoyment that way and you won't have to pay KONAMI anything.

Metal Gear Solid V is clearly an unfinished game. Its story and SIDE OPS take a complete nosedive after CHAPTER 1 (even in CHAPTER 1 they weren't exactly stellar), with the second chapter being nothing more than a bunch of repeat missions and a couple of quests that narratively completely jump the shark and feel like fragments of what should have been a game twice its length. There is no satisfying ending, no clever payoffs, nor anything of the sort. The game goes out with a whimper before any of its narrative elements coalesce into something greater.

The thing that makes me want to recommend this game to almost anyone, however, is its gameplay. MGS V is still one of the greatest open-world, single-player, tactical sandboxes I have ever played. The fact that this game gives you such absurdly varied weapons, gadgets, and tools with which you then infiltrate your way across two giant maps is nothing short of staggering. Save a hostage by going in guns blazing, stealth your way through while leaving no traces of your infiltration, call in a support heli, mount loudspeakers onto a decoy and distract half the enemy forces with it, run around as a giant box with a poster of a babe glued to the front as you then karate chop those commie bastards left, right, and center. This game truly is the wet dream of anyone who wants to try out new and wacky ways of completing any given task.

What really helps with this gameplay loop are the enemy forces. While I can't help but feel like most of them are a bit too dumb and could use a buff to their hearing, eyesight, and damage output, the thing that makes them an evergreen enemy is their adaptability. Did you infiltrate a base by mostly shooting enemies in the head? Now they receive helmets. Did you throw around sleep grenades? Now they get gas masks. Have you used a route one too many times? There might be a minefield waiting for you the next time you try the same route. Shoot them from afar with a sniper? Next time they might hav…

This one is a real head scratcher tbh. I've played it for 80+ hours and I'm not even close to losing interest. The gameplay is peak. The action is breathtaking. There are so many tools to build a play style around. Sometimes the story even makes me feel a little something, despite some awkward dialogue and characterization. It's an addictive experience. And yet stuck amongst the elegant, strategic, flawlessly-executed core of the game is a great ugly contusion of truly baffling design and story choices, which culminate in an absurdly threadbare second act devoid of anything close to narrative closure, leaving some of the game's biggest questions absurdly unresolved. Instead, one is faced with a sorry sequence of mandatory "repeat" missions--more challenging versions of earlier sections that would have made fine post game or achievement hunting content, but are in this context absolutely shameless filler. As a coherent vision, the game is simply not finished (a falling out between Kojima and Konami, apparently). I suppose this is well documented by now, but I'm here ten years too late, shaking my head anyway. At the same time, the game's primary "ranking" mechanism (how you are graded at the end of each mission) is so overwhelmingly weighted towards speed that any real incentive to execute a strategy worthy of the games tactical system disappears into a blizzard of bum-rush cheese as you plough through levels as quickly as possible, exploiting every possible loophole in the system, literally tanking checkpoints at times. Once you figure this out, some of the hardest missions suddenly become painfully easy to S Rank. But it doesn't feel good. MGS V is better than that. Again, I'm not saying I dislike the game. I love it, actually, but it's just such a shame such glaring flaws were allowed to blemish what could have been an almost flawless experience. So, what am i saying? Is it worth playing? Absolutely. Just prepare yourself for some really infuriating moments.

Kojima's last game before Konami took over. I will give a good review anyways to show respect but realistically i have mixed feeling and i feel bad saying it.

--PROS--
-Stealth mechanics are still ahead of their time, and easily i can call them the best i have ever seen
-Cutscenes may be diluted, but quality of animations and voice acting is excellent and i don't have anything bad to say.
-Access to licensed music you can collect and listen to
-Fan service, though this time it was overexaggerated, its nothing new for Kojima
-Access to recorded dialogues that can help with understanding the lore, as always over-explained not only in lore but also how things work scientifically to get a better picture
-References to previous games, i won't spoil anything here
-Mother base itself, grinding your base, assigning staff, developing, Fulton extractions, managing your buddy's

--CONS--
-BIGGEST kick in the nuts: Forcing a player to do the same mission that already happened but with a MODIFIER in order to progress the campaign. Same goes with the last mission, you literally REPLAY the first one which means unskipable crawling on the floor, the only difference is the last cutscene. In my opinion it kind of ruined the vibe of ending.
-As i mentioned before, actual campaign missions are diluted. One time actually something happens and there's a lot of going on, 
and the other time its just lots of extraction missions that SHOULD be in my opinion only in SIDE OPS missions.
RECOMMENDATION
Don't do side ops if you play this game for lore, unless you want to grind but remember you will end up with playtime like me.

NOT to mention Initialisms like: P.F DARPA XOF FOX i heard it so much and so quick in lots of dialogues my brain that speaks English as second language gets totally fried and i don't understand anything at ALL.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the opening section of the game as very slow and tedious.

citations.review_text:
Will alter this as i progress. First hour in and still pretty much hallway and waiting in FPV, dragging hard.

The constant alarm and shaky cam in tight spaces made me genuinely feel quite sick so i played on mute for a bit then alt+F4'd the game. No option to turn down any sounds. Why. 

Probably the grimmest opening of a game ive ever played. Start off getting news you are wasted away, fated to death from injuries, and missing an arm. Constant innocent people getting brutally murdered in a cold calculated attack on a hospital being burned down. The first to go is a nurse being garroted.

---

About 60 hours in. It took a little while to get there but it does open up into the game I expected when I paid for it. Very big world, lots of things to do and collect.

If you havent played Peacewalker, it's going to quite a big leap in gameplay for you. Rather than solely stealth metroidvania-lite, you also have to collect soldiers to build up your army, so you will spend a lot of time scanning, pacifying, and extracting soldiers, and dismissing soldiers that are no longer up to your standard. 

Why do this?, because in general the higher the level of your departments, the more upgrades and gear become available to you to develop, and there is a lot. Specific individuals, tied to a mission, have specific skills that change the game, for example translators so you can know what the enemy are saying, its hard to think of ones that arent spoilers though.

There is a vibe of Snake Eater since you can still tranq and collect animals, but dont think you can eat them, since you are meant to be preserving them, never tried though. Gladly no stamina watching and food management and permanent bolts. You can choose different camo, but not quickly switching them in the menu, you have to either choose it in your deployment, or have it supply dropped at a price, and there is no camo %, so its hard to tell how much difference they make, meaning ive just stuck to one the entire time. Disg…

I wont bother touching on the story.  the gameplay itself is what metal gear was always meant to be. the beginning of this game is excruciatingly slow but if you can suffer through it you wont regret it. the replay value is top tier in my opinion especially if you are interested in obtaining higher ranking on missions

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game is unfinished with cut content and a rushed final act.

citations.review_text:
The infamous lost child of the Metal Gear Solid series. Where mighty ambitions of finally bringing the series’ story full circle met the development capability to see it through, only to be tragically cut short by well-documented behind-the-scenes drama. 

Despite being the fifth numbered game in the series, MGSV has little to do with MGSIV, being instead a direct sequel to the formerly PSP exclusive Peace Walker spinoff. From which the vast majority of its writing and mechanics are taken directly from. Indeed the only major addition is the replacement of PW’s various menus with explorable open worlds.

MGSV is quite an anomaly among its kind. Most rushed and unfinished games make this label apparent as soon as you boot them up, if you even can. For MGSV’s entire first act, however, you’d be hard pressed to realize it too fell into this camp. Which is to say, despite the new game engine and additional complexities of its expanded mechanics, this machine ticks along with surprisingly few issues. Levels are generally well designed, stealth mechanics are engaging and satisfying, and there’s just enough variety and depth to keep you on your toes.

Complaints are inevitable, though, and my most common would be against the game’s vague rules regarding detection by enemies. Hopping genres into action is nothing new for the MGS series, but I found MGSV’s mechanics and design particularly poorly suited to it. Both of these though can be worked around, however. 

On a broader note, MGSV is mechanically surprisingly deep, yet most of these mechanics will rarely, if ever, come into play. There’s a complex system of communications which reaches all the way down to alert levels being raised if a soldier is interrupted while on the radio. There’s a dynamic difficulty system where enemies gain new equipment to counter specific overused strategies. There’s a full day-night cycle and variable weather, both of which influence enemy patrol and behavior. Yet none of this will st…

the game is REALLY fun but...its an unfinished product with cut content , weird pacing and repetitve mission structure . konami also shoved this game with useless online elements that u pretty much have to engage in , they also made the game technically p2w which is atrocious for a singleplayer game about grinding and making an army . new updates also make the game run worse usually ( also they added denuvo ) . konami sabotaged the creation of the best game ever made from the start but it still holds its ground as one of the greats.

After so long I have finally 100% this game. and my thoughts on it are, well its an unfinished game, I feel like there is a lot of missed potential with what this game was going to be and ended up not due to well the publisher. especially towards the end of the game and reused missions and areas, I feel like the direction it was taken was a cool concept with even more freedom to take on missions how you want to take them, but at the end of the day it just feels a little stale on the cusp of greatness to me. The enemy A.I. is either incredibly dumb or incredibly obnoxious, it's not like the previous games like MGS 2 or 3, at least in my eyes those games have a better sneaking simulation than this game did, which is probably because of the rushed release of this game. and the timers for developing items, my god what an annoyance.

However it is still a fun package nonetheless I think if you just play through the game as intended and don't focus on completing everything this game has it is a fun game, most of my playthrough I never utilized the multiple guns they had on offer here mostly due to the fact that the game favors stealth over shooting action, and the guns feel almost useless towards the end when you know what is the best. the reuse of areas really makes the world stagnant rather than alive. it's a huge departure from the previous titles in that there is no linearity in its set pieces . It just leaves me wondering what could have been. Still worth playing if you are a fan of the series and you want to follow the story.
Unfinished game, but despite that, still very enjoyable. Runs and looks great. Just a shame it could have been so much more. It is very obvious how rushed the second half of the game is.

Gave it a thumbs down because so many people were gushing over this and saying how great it was so I got it. Then after playing for a bit I found out it was a half finished game, with no real ending. Lots of filler, and you get to replay missions because the creators went their separate ways during the making of it. Even before that you go to the same area over and over again in a lifeless and dull open world that forces you to back track over the same ground again and again. Or you can take the chopper which is an unskippable sequence that you endure again and again an again. Towards the end of it I just wanted it over with and there was no joy. The worst thing was finding out the ending was replaying the extremely boring start mission. Sure there was some good parts, but not enough for a thumbs up.

Or you can take the chopper which is an unskippable sequence that you endure again and again an again. Towards the end of it I just wanted it over with and there was no joy. The worst thing was finding out the ending was replaying the extremely boring start mission. Sure there was some good parts, but not enough for a thumbs up.
